_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. The hand-authored packages internal/portal and internal/cadate, and the hand-authored command files under internal/cli (auth_login, auth_use_account, auth_cloudally_refresh, backup_*, download*, portal_session, restore*), carry no DO NOT EDIT marker, so regen-merge keeps them whole; the backstop entries below catch a reprint that drops their wiring or a review that weakens their live-API rules.

handfixes.summary: cli/NOTICE names this connector's contributor, in the Apache-2.0 attribution channel
handfixes.why: CONTRIBUTING.md promises that a contributor's credit survives a regeneration. The press regenerates cli/NOTICE from its own template, which carries the CLI Printing Press attribution but not this repo's per-connector 'contributed by' sentence, so a reprint would silently delete the only place the credit lives.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The press has no per-connector contributor field, so there is nothing to encode upstream today.

asserts.contains: The CloudAlly connector was contributed by Jeff Moore (@sonofskywalker3).

handfixes.summary: doctor classifies the authenticated GET /v2/user answer and turns the api row red on a 404 or a non-JSON answer, instead of calling every non-401/403 answer 'not verified' while the api row stays 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)'
handfixes.why: The 4.33.5 doctor probed /v2/user but left report["api"] at 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)' when every API path 404s (a base_url aimed at a web UI), so check_doctor_truth.py's wrong-base state failed: the API read as healthy. doctor_verdict.go (ported from watchguard) reports 'valid' only for a JSON object with members or a JSON array, names CLOUDALLY_BASE_URL in the wrong-base remedy, and points a 401 at auth login. check_doctor_truth.py --slug cloudally failed 1 assertion before this fix and passes after (run on Linux; on Windows the gate's 0600 chmod does not satisfy the credential-file DACL guard, which is true of every connector). See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["api"] = fmt.Sprintf("ERROR the host answered but %s is not there - %s", doctorProbePath, doctorWrongBaseHint)

handfixes.summary: the root command's Short and Long read 'CloudAlly CLI - ...' with the vendor's casing and describe restores, downloads, backup history and health
handfixes.why: The generator emitted 'Cloudally CLI' with a long-dash separator, a Short truncated mid-sentence, and a description that predates the download commands; MCP clients and --help show it.

asserts.contains: Short: `CloudAlly CLI - Restores and mailbox downloads to a past backup date

handfixes.summary: golang.org/x/text is pinned at v0.42.0 (>= 0.41.0)
handfixes.why: osv flags golang.org/x/text v0.39.0 for GO-2026-5970 and GO-2026-6629; the press go.mod template emits v0.39.0, so a reprint reintroduces it. Same pin as sonicwall and watchguard.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Ported unchanged from skills/sonicwall (same 4.33.5 template defect). Press creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string; the converter renders the built-in local Administrator as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched and every credential read was refused. The fix resolves each trustee to its SID and compares SIDs; the allow-list is unchanged.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl. Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

asserts.contains: func trusteeSID(trustee string, resolveAlias sddlAliasResolver) string {

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL rendered flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL) is refused
handfixes.why: Ported unchanged from skills/sonicwall (same 4.33.5 template defect). Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, but SDDL puts DACL flags first, so a world-accessible token file was accepted.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates and upstream issue as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: manifest.json names the MCP server and its entry point cloudally-mcp, not cloudally-pp-mcp
handfixes.why: The press manifest uses the -pp- binary names; a re-onboard that re-derives name / entry_point / mcp_config.command from it points the .mcpb at a binary the release build never emits.

handfixes.summary: every operator variable the binaries read is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md, with CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_ID and CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_SECRET required and CLOUDALLY_ACCESS_TOKEN optional and blank
handfixes.why: The press manifest declared only CLOUDALLY_ACCESS_TOKEN and the four login inputs, but every request also needs the client-id and client-secret headers, so a Claude Desktop install was never prompted for the two values it cannot work without. A pasted access token expires and then overrides the token auth login saved and refreshes, so the docs tell operators to leave it blank and run auth login once.

handfixes.summary: the generated auth command registers the hand-authored `auth use-account`
handfixes.why: auth use-account mints an account-scoped token from the partner login (POST .../partner-access-token) and swaps it in, which is how a partner acts inside one customer. Its command file is hand-authored and survives a reprint, but the AddCommand line lives in the generated auth.go, so a reprint silently drops the subcommand.

handfixes.summary: the async-job wait on distributor-account-tasks get, reseller-accounts backup-statuses and user status polls /v2/backup-tasks/{id} and names `tasks get <id>` as the recovery command
handfixes.why: The generator wires --wait on these commands to a sibling status endpoint and may pick /v2/resellers/accounts/{accountId}/backup-tasks/{id} or /v2/distributors/accounts/{accountId}/backup-tasks/{id}. WaitForJob substitutes only {id}, so {accountId} reaches the wire unsubstituted, and the printed recovery hint named `jobs get`, which reads the CLI's own local job table rather than CloudAlly. /v2/backup-tasks/{id} takes only the task id and `tasks get` is the matching read.

handfixes.summary: downloads are created through the customer portal's startRestoreOrDownload with a constant job type EXPORT, never the documented recovery/export endpoint
handfixes.why: Live, 2026-10-15: POST .../recovery/export answers 200 with an empty body and creates no job, so the generated recovery export commands cannot create a download. The portal endpoint creates one, but it also accepts RESTORE (writes into the live mailbox) and DELETEITEMS (deletes from the backup), so the type is a package constant, never taken from a caller. Backstop for hand-authored files.

handfixes.summary: download start refuses an MS365 task and points at download submit
handfixes.why: Live, 2026-10-15: an MS365 mailbox downloads as one job per sub-source (O365MAIL, O365CALENDAR, O365CONTACTS, O365TASKS, O365NOTES), each asked for with that sub-source's own timestamp; a job for the parent MS365 source is accepted by the portal and creates nothing. download submit resolves the per-sub-source timestamps; download start resolves one run timestamp, so it refuses MS365 rather than report a job that never exists.

handfixes.summary: download submit --utc-offset selects backups by the account's own calendar day (Resolver.RunOnLocalDate)
handfixes.why: Live, 2026-10-15: CloudAlly stamps snapshots in UTC and a nightly backup that runs late in the evening local time is stamped the next UTC day, so selecting the UTC date 2022-12-31 for a US Eastern account delivered the 30 December state. RunOnLocalDate reads the UTC window for the local day, which can straddle two calendar months. Backstop for hand-authored files.

asserts.contains: func (r *Resolver) RunOnLocalDate(ctx context.Context, ent Entity, day time.Time, offset time.Duration) (Snapshot, bool, error) {

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md carry the live CloudAlly facts an agent needs: portal-only past dates and extid, UTC stamps, the no-op export endpoint, per-sub-source MS365 downloads, 60-second links, never deleting a backup task for a download job, and spacing parallel portal sessions
handfixes.why: A re-onboard regenerates these docs from the press templates, which know only the documented API. Every fact here was observed against a production partner tenant on 2026-10-15, and an agent without them deletes data (DELETE backup-tasks on a download job id), delivers the wrong day's mail (UTC stamps), or reports success for jobs that do not exist (recovery export, parent-MS365 downloads).

asserts.contains: **Never point a delete at a download job.**

handfixes.summary: The store keys backup-statuses rows by userId+taskId+source+entityName, so sync stores them and backup health has rows to read
handfixes.why: The backup-statuses feed carries no id field (spec types V2EntityStatusDirectView / V2EntityStatus3TierView, and the shapes seen live). The 4.33.5 store found no identity, so sync stored 0 rows, exited 1, and backup health printed [] (exit 0), which an agent reads as every backup healthy. Found by the PR #400 docs review against a stub feed. The composite override uses the store's native a+b override syntax; TestBackupStatusRowsStoreWithoutID fails without it.

handfixes.summary: tasks get's Example selects entity,status, the keys it actually emits
handfixes.why: tasks get unwraps the response to the entities array, so the generated Example --select entities.entity,entities.status matched no fields and exited 2. Found by the PR #400 docs review.

handfixes.summary: auth logout and auth set-token delete auth-context.json (the partner access and refresh token) and fail loudly if they cannot
handfixes.why: auth login --partner keeps the partner tokens in <state>/auth-context.json so auth use-account can switch customers. The 4.33.5 logout cleared only credentials.toml, so after logout `auth use-account --partner` restored a working partner session (every customer) with no password. Found by the PR #400 runtime review; TestLogoutRemovesPartnerSidecar fails without these lines. auth.go is generated, so a reprint drops them.

handfixes.summary: The local store (restore ledger, synced feeds) is keyed by API origin + client id + logged-in principal through config.StoreScopeIdentity, not by the rotating access token
handfixes.why: The template names the store after a hash of the auth header. CloudAlly tokens rotate on every refresh and re-login, so each rotation opened an empty store: restore history vanished and `restore submit --resume` advised starting a new batch, which resends restores that may already have been accepted. Origin + client id alone let a company login open the partner's store, so the principal is part of the key. Backstop: a template change that ignores the hook brings the token-named stores back silently.

handfixes.summary: Login, refresh and use-account POSTs refuse every redirect; the portal session refuses a redirect off its origin or to http; generated clients refuse to replay a body across origins
handfixes.why: A cross-host 307 sent client-id, client-secret and the password or refresh token to the foreign host, and the CLI saved the token that host returned (PR #400 runtime review, reproduced against stubs). The portal client forwarded X-CSRF-TOKEN the same way. Backstop for hand-written files.

handfixes.summary: download fetch writes owner-only folders and files inside --dest, never through a link, never over an existing file, only from https links to public hosts; download submit records ambiguous creates as UNKNOWN
handfixes.why: Archives were written 0644/0755, a planted .partial symlink redirected the write outside --dest, an existing archive was silently replaced, any server-supplied URL was fetched (SSRF), and a create that timed out was resent on --resume (PR #400 review). Backstop for hand-written files.

handfixes.summary: import is CLI-only and the teach/teach-playbook file flags are refused over MCP, so no MCP tool reads or writes a local file the caller names
handfixes.why: Under CLOUDALLY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1, teach_playbook --notes-file read credentials.toml and playbook_list returned the access token (PR #400 round-2 runtime review); import --input read any JSONL file and POSTed a create per line. teach.go, teach_playbook.go and import.go are generated (fleet-wide 4.33.5 template), so a reprint drops these annotations. TestMCPLocalFileFlagsBlocked walks every MCP-visible command and fails on any unblocked file/path flag.

handfixes.summary: Local stores are keyed by API origin + CloudAlly user (not token, not key pair); the restore ledger commands fail closed on an unusable auth-context.json; the portal URL must be https
handfixes.why: Round 2 of the PR #400 review: every partner login shared one principal, so a restricted partner user opened the administrator's cached data; rotating the key pair orphaned the ledger; a refused or legacy sidecar silently opened an empty per-token store and restore history read as empty; CLOUDALLY_PORTAL_URL=http://... sent the single-use handoff token in cleartext. Backstop for hand-written files.

asserts.contains: func partnerPrincipal(email string) string { return principalPartnerPrefix + userKey(email) }
